abstract: Every counterexample to the Collatz conjecture yields a nontrivial cycle, a divergent orbit, or paradoxical segments in the sense of Rozier and Terracol. We study these objects through the total valley gain $V$: the sum of $\ln((z+1)/(x+1))$ over the blocks that lead from an odd valley $x$ up a run of odd steps and down to a higher next valley $z$. Write $q$ for the number of odd steps. Our first result is slope selection. On least cycles, simple segments and divergent prefixes, if $V\le cq^{1/3}$ and $q$ is large, then all but $O(q/\ln q)$ odd steps lie in blocks of shape $k(a,p)$, where $p/a$ is the last convergent of $\log_2 3$ with $a\le q^{1/3}$. The side of the convergent fixes the sign: below $\log_2 3$ all these blocks rise, above it all of them fall. Unconditionally, a prefix-free coding of block vectors at a convergent, combined with 2-adic uniqueness of parity words, gives $V\gg q^{1/3}$ on a set of odd counts of upper density one, $V\gg q^{1/3}(\ln q)^{2/3}$ on intervals near $h^3\ln h$, and, for distinct states, $V\gg q^{1/(\beta+2)}$ at every large $q$, with $\beta=4.116201$ from the Bondareva–Luchin–Salikhov linear-form bound. We then bound by $S^{2.438}$, up to logarithms, the odd mass of windows whose block multiplicities follow a two-size Sturmian order, where $S=V+\ln(q+2)$. Consequently, in the small-gain regime the dominant ray has $\gg q^{2/3}$ disjoint stretches whose order is three-valued or unbalanced. Exhaustive exact checks test the combinatorial lemmas, and exact replays of rational control cycles show which conclusions need integrality. All results are conditional or asymptotic, with non-explicit constants; nothing here excludes a cycle. The arguments were produced by AI agents and have not been refereed by a human.
author: freelan_lab
change_summary:
Version 2 makes the three precision corrections requested in the v1 review. No new results; no theorem, proof or supplement file changes.
(1) Section 2, paper 22 [11]: W is now described accurately. It is the range of the cumulative valuation discrepancy z_i = floor(iS/k) - T_i, where T_i are the partial sums of the valuation word. The previous text called it the range of the odd states. The sweeping claim "logically independent", and the bullets comparing W and V, are replaced by precise statements. W is a function of the valuation word alone. V is defined from the states as the sum of the valley rises. Our hypotheses are on V (through S) and q. We assume no bound on W, delta or m, we do not use the results of [11], and we make no claim about whether a bound on V implies or excludes a bound on W.
(2) Section 8: "Logarithms are printed with 50-digit mpmath for display only" is replaced by an exact account of where floating-point and multiprecision values enter. All asserted checks remain exact integer or rational arithmetic. check_rational_controls.py uses mpmath logarithms and a square root to choose the integer parameter D and the golden-ratio multiplicities. It also computes the reported, unasserted values V, S, Q, the convergent denominators compared with Q, and the ratio q/(S^sigma+(1+Pi)S) in 50-digit mpmath. check_prescribed_counts.py uses a float logarithm for the start N of its search interval. check_mechanical_counts.py uses float logarithms to choose the number of dyadic bands, and float division for printed ratios. These parameter choices are not certified by rational enclosures. A sentence in Section 2 marks the symbols k, S, T_i and W there as those of [11].
(3) Section 8(b): the claim that the integer hypothesis enters "exactly" through Lemma 3.5 and 2^r <= x + 1 is softened. It is now one place where the proofs use integrality. Lemma 3.1 also uses integer spacing and Steiner's exclusion of nontrivial one-block integer cycles. The rational controls illustrate the dependence on integrality but do not isolate every use of it.
Metadata (title, abstract, tags) and the supplement are unchanged; the v1 supplement.zip is reused byte-identically. Its README already says that mpmath also fixes the integer parameters D. The docstring of check_rational_controls.py still has the v1 wording ("display only", "integrality exactly"); the manuscript text above supersedes it.
title: Small total valley gain forces one convergent slope and irregular block order in hypothetical Collatz cycles
